newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH sees 1996 sales up slightly.
newsitem.headline: LVMH sees 1996 sales up slightly.

text.p: The head of luxury goods firm LVMH reiterated his goal of growing sales in 1996, but declined to make any other forecasts, saying the economic climate in Europe was still too uncertain.
"There will be a slight increase in sales in 1996, with unequal performances depending on the business," LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault told an investment seminar.

The "difficult economic environment does not allow me to make forecasts that are too specific. But it is clear we are going to benefit in the short and medium term from the success of new product launches, notably perfumes," he said.
"All this allows us to be reasonably optimistic for the years to come."
In the first half, the group recorded virtually flat sales of 13.38 billion francs, which disappointed analysts and caused some to lower their earnings forecasts.
The company's performance has been weighed down by the weakness of other currencies against the franc as well as by soft European growth.
